params.body:
**Part 3 of 3, stacked on #368 and #369 (merge those first; until they merge this diff shows their 110 files too).** One push of 170 files exceeds the control gateway's 60-second budget for a GitHub effect (four attempts timed out at the tree or the commit step), so the migrated files went in two pure-addition parts and this part carries the last 17 findings, the 24 open points, the READMEs, the generator, the test and the deletion of the two tables.

## Why

Every pull request tonight appended a row to `docs/bedrijfsregels/90-x-bevindingen.md` (and sometimes `91-o-open-punten.md`). Two appends at the end of one file always conflict in git; two agents choosing "the next free number" never conflict but collide silently (X-109 to X-111 landed twice on 14 September). Result: more than ten rebase rounds in twelve hours, and six green PRs (356, 358, 359, 360, 361, 362) all conflicting on that one file. `RulesIdentityTest` (PR 353) made the collisions loud; this makes them impossible.

## What

- `docs/bedrijfsregels/bevindingen/`: one file per finding, `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`, frontmatter (`id` for migrated rows only, `titel`, `ernst`, `regel`, `status`, `gevonden`, `opgelost`, `beslist`, `waar`) and the two prose cells as paragraphs. `docs/bedrijfsregels/open-punten/`: the same for open points, without `ernst`/`regel`. Each directory has a README with the layout and the schema.
- **Identity.** A new finding has no number; it is referred to by its file name (`bevinding: <slug>` in a docblock or chapter). The 127 migrated findings and 24 open points keep `id: X-nn` / `id: O-nn`, so every existing reference (tests, chapters, open points) still resolves. Nothing is renumbered.
- `bin/rules-split-findings`: the one-off conversion, kept in the repo because it documents which cell became which field. Both table shapes of the findings file are read (the open table with seven cells; the resolved table, which had grown three shapes: four, six and seven cells). Dates come from the row text where it says "Gevonden op ..." / "Opgelost op ..."; otherwise `2026-09-11`, the day the catalogue was frozen (the README says so).
- `bin/rules-findings.php`: the shared reader (one `key: value` per line, no YAML library, since a value may start with a backtick), used by `bin/rules-page`, the split script and the test.
- `bin/rules-page` reads the two directories instead of the tables and renders open and resolved findings apart (with dates); the open-points block is unchanged in content. `bin/rules-coverage` never read the findings; only its header comment changes.
- `RulesIdentityTest`: uniqueness of `id` across frontmatter, every `X-nn`/`O-nn` reference in `docs/` and `tests/` resolves to a file's `id`, every `bevinding: <slug>` / `open punt: <slug>` reference resolves to a file (with or without the date prefix), frontmatter fields present and `ernst`/`status` from the allowed set. `RulesDocsBuildTest` and `RulesCoverageTest` stay green.
- The intro, `CLAUDE.md` (Business rules section), `docs/acceptatietest.md` and the docblocks that named the old file now point at the directory.

## Checked

- 127 findings (75 open, 52 resolved) and 24 open points written; the two old files deleted.
- Spot-checked by hand against the original rows: X-02, X-44 (ernst `opgelost` in the open table becomes `status: opgelost`), X-87 (long `waar` cell with semicolons), X-117 (six-cell resolved row), X-126 (four-cell resolved row), X-74, O-04.
- `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter 'RulesIdentity|RulesDocsBuild|RulesCoverage'`: 9 tests, 16 assertions, OK. The page renders 127 findings and 24 open points (checked in jsdom).

## For the PRs still in flight

Write new findings as files in `bevindingen/` with exactly the frontmatter in the README (no `id`), and refer to them as `bevinding: <slug>`. The six waiting PRs are restacked on this one in follow-up PRs marked "(restacked)".
params.title: Findings and open points: one file each, so parallel work stops colliding (part 3 of 3)
